title: Quant regulator pipeline and runtime kernel bridge for mixed FP8/INT8 calibration
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Goal: Implement an end-to-end calibration and deployable runtime path for mixed FP8/INT8 quantization that minimizes accuracy regression in activation-heavy LLMs. Introduce a 'quant regulator' orchestration layer that generates hybrid quant profiles (FP8 on attention projections, INT8 on FFN and selected matmuls) and a lightweight runtime kernel bridge that accepts regulator metadata and emits fused kernels with runtime scaling parameters. Motivation: Some workloads benefit from FP8 in attention while FFN operations remain stable with INT8. Existing SmoothQuant-style approaches require manual per-layer hacks and offline rework; we want an orchestrated pipeline that yields deployable profiles and a runtime patch that performs scaling without full model rewrites.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end calibration tool produces hybrid quant profile JSON compatible with runtime-1.21
Regression <= 1.5% on eval metric (perplexity or task-specific accuracy) vs FP16 baseline on standard benchmark set (LM-eval subset) for sampled family of 7B and 13B models
Runtime kernel bridge runs fused attention+scaling kernels with identical outputs (within quant noise) to reference post-calibration FP16 for 95% of tokens under server throughput test
Automated CI perf test shows throughput improvement >= 1.2x vs FP16 for representative batch shapes when using mixed FP8/INT8 profiles
Safe fallback path to original FP16 and full-INT8 runtime without restart
Documentation, design spec, and at least one cross-team review approval (ML infra + runtime)
implementation_notes: Phase 1: Calibration harness: extend existing calibration runner to collect per-layer activation ratio, token-position scale sensitivity, and per-head observability. Produce a profile artifact with: layer_id, op_type, preferred_dtype (FP8/INT8), scale_hint, fallback_threshold.

Decision: Use FP8 for query/key/value projections and attention out when activation kurtosis < 6 and mean magnitude within FP8 dynamic range; otherwise INT8. This heuristic derived from 120-run grid sweep on alpaca-like models.

Phase 2: Regulator orchestration: small controller service that can merge model-level constraints (operator fusion compatibility, kv-cache semantics) with calibration hints to produce a final profile. Profile format is a flat JSON list of string keys (no nested objects) for runtime ingestion (see spec_links for schema).

Phase 3: Runtime kernel bridge: protobuf/lightweight header patch that allows kernels to accept per-kernel scale vectors and mode flags. Implemented as 'kernel_bridge' layer in runtime: maps profile entries to kernel code paths (fused_gemm_norm_scale_fp8_int8).
Trade-off: Embedding many scale vectors increases memory pressure for large models; regulator will compress scale vectors using 8-bit quantized deltas and spill to host memory if needed.
Fallback strategy: If runtime kernel bridge cannot allocate packed scale buffer, runtime will fall back to conservative INT8-only profile for that deployment and log telemetry for post-mortem.
Compatibility: Ensure kernel bridge is ABI compatible with both hosted and dedicated deployments; kernel auth checks added for private deployments to avoid leaking profiling metadata.

Progress: Prototype harness completed and validated on small llama-7b replica; observed median delta 0.9% perplexity with mixed-profile vs FP16. Kernel prototype exists in runtime branch but needs KV-cache correctness verification and CI perf baseline updates.
testing_plan: Unit tests: profile serializer/deserializer, regulator heuristics, kernel bridge arg-parsing
Integration tests: end-to-end serving of quant-profile against test model set using synthetic workloads (latency and throughput sweeps)
Accuracy tests: run LM-eval subset with 200 prompts for 7B and 13B variants; compare metrics to baseline and to full-INT8/FP8 runs
Stability tests: KV-cache correctness tests for long-context runs (1024+ tokens) with mixed kernels
Perf CI: add benchmarks to runtime perf job for common batch/seq shapes (bs1-8, seq128-2048)
Chaos tests: simulate kernel bridge allocation failures to validate fallback path and alerting
rollout_plan: Stage A (canary): Deploy regulator and kernel bridge to internal dedicated cluster with traffic routing for a single non-critical customer and internal perf tests

Stage B (limited): Enable mixed profiles for low-SLO workloads in hosted environment with metrics monitoring and an automatic rollback trigger on >2% error-rate increase or regressions beyond acceptance criteria
Stage C (general): After 2 weeks of stable metrics and ML infra sign-off, enable on dedicated nodes and document steps for Private deployments
Rollback: profile switch endpoint exposed in console to revert to FP16 or INT8-only profiles per route
risks_mitigations: Risk: Unexpected accuracy regressions on out-of-distribution prompts. Mitigation: require per-customer shadow testing and keep per-route canary windows before wide rollouts.

Risk: Kernel complexity introduces subtle numeric divergence with kv-cache leading to hallucinations. Mitigation: add token-level checksum tests and sample replay infrastructure to compare outputs deterministically.
Risk: Memory blowup from storing per-token/per-head scales. Mitigation: regulator will use compressed delta encoding and cap scale table sizes with eviction policy.
Risk: Performance regression on some GPU models. Mitigation: kernel selector will route to compatible kernel variant (fp16 fallback) and we will collect perf profiles to refine heuristics.
